course.title: Financial Technology
course.prerequisites: WAD301 Web App Development for Data Science (with Streamlit & FastAPI/Flask) MAD302 Mobile App Development for Data Science (Android & ML Integration) IDS101 Introduction to Data Science and Engineering BIA301 Business Intelligence and Analytics
course.description: The evolution of finance and technology has been closely linked throughout history, beginning with the earliest coins and extending to contemporary cryptocurrencies. In the past decade, the rapid pace of change, coupled with a growing array of new entrants—including startups, technology firms, and participants from both global and emerging markets—has significantly transformed the financial landscape. This course targets individuals engaged in finance, technology, regulation, or FinTech, as well as students of related disciplines and those seeking to expand their knowledge of a significant contemporary process. Students will develop a deeper understanding of the key trends in finance, technology, and regulation, equipping them to navigate both opportunities and risks, including those affecting traditional financial institutions, business models, and their personnel.

clos.description: Discuss the nature of financial technology, and relevant areas such as historical evolution, development, application, governance, entrepreneurship, ethics and regulatory landscape
Analyse the industry trend by knowing who is driving innovation and how FinTech will have a lasting impact on economies, markets, companies and individuals
Critically evaluate technology innovation in finance and major technological trends, including digital finance, alternative finance, cryptos, blockchain, AI and big data
Articulate the fundamental roles of data, security, digital transformation as well as their implication on financial services
Experiment data science applications in finance using sample projects

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction to Financial Technology
topics.llosRaw: Define Financial Technology, and its characteristics Explain the historical context of FinTech's emergence Analyze how FinTech challenges traditional banking Outline the key domains of the financial services sector currently being disrupted by FinTech

topics.title: Topic 2: Financial Services and Products
topics.llosRaw: Outline the fundamental functions of traditional financial institutions Contrast the traditional product-centric approach with the FinTech Categorize and describe how new FinTech models Explain how customer behavior models derived from FinTechs are leading to new types of banking experiences

topics.title: Topic 3: Digital Finance and Alternative Finance
topics.llosRaw: Analyze the concept of digital finance, emphasizing the role of digital experiences in service delivery Evaluate specific alternative finance models, including peer-to-peer (P2P) lending and crowdfunding Discuss the competitive advantage of digital challenger banks Explain how digital currencies (like Bitcoin) arise as value stores

topics.title: Topic 4: FinTech Regulation
topics.llosRaw: Critically evaluate the challenges posed by legacy regulations to the agile and technology-driven financial services sector Define and explain the importance of RegTech and SupTech in guiding the evolution of regulatory strategy Analyze key regulatory initiatives, such as the Payment Services Directive 2 (PSD2) Discuss the strategic implications for FinTechs in managing regulatory compliance

topics.title: Topic 5: Ethics of Finance, Security and Privacy
topics.llosRaw: Analyze the implications of security and privacy in FinTech Evaluate the ethical dilemmas arising from the increasing use of big data and artificial intelligence in financial decision-making Describe emerging security solutions such as behavioural biometrics as a new era of security Explain how FinTech platforms can utilize technologies like blockchain to secure KYC information and prevent duplicating identities, thereby enhancing security and transparency

topics.title: Topic 6: Artificial Intelligent/Machine Learning and FinTech
topics.llosRaw: Explain the foundational concepts of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and deep learning in finance. Identify the broad areas where AI/ML impacts banking Analyze the function of AI-driven tools Discuss how FinTechs leverage AI/ML algorithms

topics.title: Topic 7: Data Science Applications in Finance
topics.llosRaw: Illustrate how data science and predictive algorithms are applied to achieve real-time risk analysis and generate actionable insights Showcase the use of analytics platforms that enhance transparency in lending markets by generating reports Evaluate how cognitive computing platforms use real-time data analysis to build and continually update customer risk profiles, addressing Know Your Customer (KYC) requirements and predicting threats Demonstrate how FinTechs are capitalizing on the opportunity to lend to creditworthy people who lack traditional credit

topics.title: Topic 8: Data Analytics and Regulation
topics.llosRaw: Recognize data as the "new oil of the emerging digital economy" and articulate how data science functions as a core discovery capability Characterize the complex features of Big Data in a financial context Describe how Big Data technologies and analytics are essential for building next-generation compliance and risk management systems (RegTech) Examine the critical requirement for data in regulatory environments

topics.title: Topic 9: Demystifying blockchain and DLT
topics.llosRaw: Define Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) and blockchain, emphasizing its functions Identify and explain the essential components of blockchain technologies, platforms, applications, and governance Evaluate the structural implications and non-finance applications of DLT Discuss the evolution of DLT toward platforms tailored for financial systems, such as DeFi and Web 3.0

topics.title: Topic 10: Demystifying cryptocurrencies and CBDCs
topics.llosRaw: Trace the origin of cryptocurrency to Bitcoin and blockchain technology Describe the features of cryptocurrencies (such as Altcoins) and how they challenge the traditional currency Analyze the role of cryptocurrencies in global transactions, such as using Bitcoin as an intermediate currency for low-cost, high-speed cross-border currency exchange and instant payment Recognize the new risks associated with virtual currencies

topics.title: Topic 11: Mini Project
topics.llosRaw: Synthesize core concepts of data science, and FinTech business models to define and structure a novel solution for a complex financial industry challenge Experiment the application of data science techniques to create personalized experiences or generate competitive insights in a chosen area (e.g., lending, payments, or investment) Propose and justify a FinTech solution that addresses a specific customer need while considering the necessary components for deployment, including ethical implications

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
